title: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e, 9.1 Verifying Trigonometric Identities and Using Trigonometric Identities to Simplify Trigonometric Expressions: Verify the fundamental trigonometric identities.
summary: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e, 9.1 Verifying Trigonometric Identities and Using Trigonometric Identities to Simplify Trigonometric Expressions: Verify the fundamental trigonometric identities.
body: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e, section "9.1 Verifying Trigonometric Identities and Using Trigonometric Identities to Simplify Trigonometric Expressions", prints these objectives: "Verify the fundamental trigonometric identities." "Simplify trigonometric expressions using algebra and the identities.". The section text says: "In espionage movies, we see international spies with multiple passports, each claiming a different identity. However, we know that each of those passports represents the same person. The trigonometric identities act in a similar manner to multiple passports—there are many ways to represent the same trigonometric expression. Just as a spy will choose an Italian passport when traveling to Italy, we choose the identity that applies to the given scenario when solving a trigonometric equation." This card reports that page. The objectives are the book's learning statements, not a separate proof.
